amending_instruments.note_en: The amendment stated on the cover page of the current Arabic PDF published by CMA -- the only amendment the cover states. The published consolidated text carries NO per-article footnotes identifying which articles the amendment changed, so NO article is flagged معدلة in this track; see known_unresolved_discrepancies.

verification_methodology_note:
TIER 1 -- TWO INDEPENDENT OFFICIAL SOURCES.

PRIMARY: the official Arabic PDF published by the issuing authority itself, fetched this pass at https://cma.gov.sa/RulesRegulations/Regulations/Documents/RULES_ON_THE_OFFER_OF_SECURITIES_AND_CONTINUING_OBLIGATIONS_ar2026.pdf (HTTP 200, 296-page born-digital PDF, 2,731,104 bytes; cma.org.sa serves the same file and 301-redirects to cma.gov.sa). Its own cover page states: issued by the CMA Board under Resolution No. 2017-123-3 dated 1439/4/9H (27/12/2017G), pursuant to the Capital Market Law (Royal Decree M/30, 1424/6/2H), AS AMENDED by CMA Board Resolution No. 2026-6-3 dated 1447/07/30H (19/01/2026G). Every Arabic character stored in this artifact comes from that file's own glyphs.

INDEPENDENT OFFICIAL CROSS-CHECK: جريدة أم القرى (Umm Al-Qura), the Kingdom's official gazette, at https://www.uqn.gov.sa/decisions-and-regulations/4001355 (fetched this pass, HTTP 200), which publishes the same consolidated text and states the identical citation and identical amending resolution. This is a different publisher from CMA, so the two are independent official witnesses.

ARTICLE COUNT: 112, verified three ways -- (a) the PDF's own table of contents (pages 2-8) ends at المادة الثانية عشرة بعد المائة: النشر والنفاذ; (b) the body (pages 11-98) contains exactly 112 blue-set article headings forming a clean 1..112 run with no gaps and no مكرر article; (c) the Umm Al-Qura text contains the same 112 headings. This confirms the figure reported by the corpus census.

TEXT-LAYER RECONSTRUCTION (why a plain pdftotext of this file is unusable): the PDF places every glyph individually in VISUAL order and uses Arabic ligature glyphs whose ToUnicode entries expand to 2-3 letters. Any ordinary extractor therefore transposes the letters inside every ligature (المملكة -> اململكة, المالية -> املالية) and scatters digits and punctuation. Text was rebuilt at glyph level from MuPDF's raw glyph trace: (1) a ligature's continuation characters (glyph id -1, degenerate box at the lead glyph's origin) are rejoined in the order the font's OWN ToUnicode declares -- 50 distinct multi-character mappings were harvested from the file's 14 ToUnicode streams and nothing outside that declared set is ever reordered; (2) zero-advance combining marks are re-attached to the base glyph their real ink box overlaps; (3) clusters are ordered right-to-left by x and maximal Latin/digit runs re-reversed; (4) the fonts' justification-filler (kashida) glyph, which they map to U+0627 but draw at ~0.10em against ~0.19-0.24em for a real alef, is dropped -- without this it injects alefs that are not in the text (المشاركين -> المشااركين). Every output character is the font's own ToUnicode value for a glyph actually drawn on the page. No word list, no spell-correction, no reconstruction from English.

INDEPENDENT VALIDATION OF THAT RECONSTRUCTION: all 112 articles were compared word-by-word against the Umm Al-Qura text after a normalisation that strips tashkeel, unifies alef/ya/ta-marbuta forms and ignores punctuation and numeral presentation. 105 of 112 articles are WORD-IDENTICAL. The 7 that are not are listed individually in known_unresolved_discrepancies; every one of them is a one- or two-word typographic divergence between the two official publications (most of them apparent typos in CMA's own PDF), NOT an extraction failure. Selected passages and the cover page were additionally verified against rendered page images.

ARABIC GOVERNS. The English CMA PDF of the same instrument exists and was NOT used to produce, correct or reconstruct any Arabic character in this artifact.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: The published consolidated text is the text AS AMENDED by CMA Board Resolution 2026-6-3 (1447/07/30H = 19/01/2026G), stated on its cover page and confirmed by Umm Al-Qura. However NEITHER official source carries per-article footnotes or markers identifying WHICH articles that resolution changed, and no pre-amendment official text was reachable this pass (web.archive.org is blocked from this network). Therefore every article is recorded as اصلية and NONE is flagged معدلة. This is a deliberate refusal to guess: the instrument IS a consolidated amended text (consolidated_amended_law = true), but the amendment cannot be attributed to individual articles from anything actually fetched. Do not read the 112 اصلية statuses as a claim that no article was amended.

Article 6, paragraph (a)(3)(ط): the CMA PDF reads 'ممثلاً لحاملي أدوت الدين' -- 'أدوت' is missing an alef and is not a word. Umm Al-Qura reads 'أدوات الدين'. The CMA PDF's own text layer is reproduced verbatim (an independent pdftotext run of the same file produces the same 'أدوت'), so this is a typo in the issuing authority's published PDF, not an extraction error. NOT silently corrected.

Article 26: the CMA PDF reads 'مدة لا تقل عن عشرة سنوات'; Umm Al-Qura reads 'عشر سنوات' (the grammatically correct form). Stored as the CMA PDF prints it. Divergence unresolved between the two official publications.
Article 53: the CMA PDF reads 'مالم تكن تلك الصفقة' (missing word space) and 'جزء من صفقة تمويل'; Umm Al-Qura reads 'ما لم' and 'جزءاً'. Stored as the CMA PDF prints it.

Article 62: the CMA PDF reads 'والمواد السابعة والستين الثامنة والستين والتاسعة والستين'; Umm Al-Qura reads '... السابعة والستين والثامنة والستين ...' (with the conjunction). Stored as the CMA PDF prints it.

Article 65, sub-paragraphs (20) and (21): the CMA PDF reads 'بافتتاح أي جراء من إجراءات الإفلاس' ('جراء' missing its hamzated alef) and 'للمُصدربموجب نظام الإفلاس' (missing word space); Umm Al-Qura reads 'أي إجراء' and 'للمُصدر بموجب'. An independent pdftotext run of the CMA file reproduces 'أي جراء', confirming the defect is in the published PDF. Stored as the CMA PDF prints it.
Article 34 heading: CMA prints 'الطلبات المعلقة'; Umm Al-Qura's web text prints 'الطلبات المعلق'. Here the defect is on the GAZETTE side; the CMA form is stored.

Article 2(a) and the cover page: the CMA PDF prints Hijri and Gregorian dates year-group first ('1424/6/2هـ', '1439/4/9هـ', '2017/12/27م') and the board resolution as '2017-123-3'; Umm Al-Qura prints the same dates and resolution in the reverse group order ('2/6/1424هـ', '9/4/1439هـ', '3-123-2017'). The article text is stored exactly as the CMA PDF renders it (confirmed against the rendered page image, glyph x-coordinates read directly). The metadata fields of this artifact use the conventional day/month/year form 9/4/1439 for the same date. Note that Umm Al-Qura's web page additionally mangles multi-digit numerals inside the running text (20% appears as 02%, 50% as 05%, 123 as 321); the CMA PDF's rendering was confirmed correct against page images, so this cross-check class of difference was excluded from the article comparison as presentation, not substance.

Optional Arabic vocalisation marks (tashkeel) are reproduced exactly as the PDF's own ToUnicode declares them. In a limited number of words the fonts declare a shadda glyph as the pair U+0651 U+064D (shadda + kasratan) where the printed page shows shadda with a different vowel or none at all -- e.g. 'يُعَدٍّ' for what the gazette writes 'يُعَدّ', and similarly 'يعدٍّل', 'وردٍّ', 'يخلٍّ'. These marks were NOT altered, because correcting them would require guessing at the intended vocalisation. Where the same glyph is drawn twice (a combined shadda+tanween glyph plus a standalone tanween glyph at the same origin) the exact duplicate mark on one base letter is collapsed; that is the only mark-level normalisation performed. Consumers who do not need tashkeel should strip U+064B-U+0652 before matching.

The source PDF renders digits and the percent sign with Arabic-Indic shapes (١٢٣, ٪) but its fonts' ToUnicode maps them to the ASCII characters U+0030-U+0039 and U+0025. The ASCII characters are stored, i.e. the characters the document itself declares, not the shapes it draws. Umm Al-Qura uses Arabic-Indic codepoints for the same digits.

The instrument's thirteenth Part (الباب الثالث عشر: الملاحق) contains 38 annexes (Annexes 1-30 plus eight lettered variants) over pages 99-296 of the source PDF -- roughly two thirds of the document. Annexes are not numbered articles and are NOT ingested by this track; only the 112 articles are. If the annex content is needed it must be built as its own, separately validated layer.

The source PDF is fully justified and pads words with elongation (kashida) glyphs. Two families occur: glyphs the fonts map to U+0640 TATWEEL, and glyphs the fonts wrongly map to U+0627 ALEF while drawing them at ~0.10em against ~0.19-0.24em for a real alef. Both are pure presentation and both are dropped -- 173 glyph drops over the whole 296-page file (166 U+0640, 7 U+0627 fillers). Keeping the U+0627 family would inject letters that are not in the text (المشاركين would be stored as المشااركين); keeping the U+0640 family would leave in-word tatweel that no Arabic word contains. The 0.15em cut separates two populations with no overlap anywhere in the file, so it is measured, not tuned. Word content is unaffected -- confirmed by the gazette cross-check, in which 105 of 112 articles come out word-identical.

Article text preserves the source PDF's own hard line breaks (the document is justified and hyphen-free, so lines break mid-sentence). No reflow was attempted, because inferring paragraph boundaries would be an editorial act. Consumers should collapse whitespace before display or matching.
